name: FTI Consulting, Inc.
warningSignals: Elevated leverage ratio (net debt/EBITDA ~2.8x) constrains M&A optionality; refinancing risk if rates remain elevated through 2025
Litigation and disputes segment revenue concentration (~28% of total) creates earnings volatility tied to case settlement cycles and client budget cycles
Talent retention in high-margin practices (forensics, restructuring) remains competitive; wage inflation in top-tier consultant labor market
opportunitySignals: Regulatory complexity expansion (AI governance, ESG compliance, sanctions screening) driving demand for specialized advisory; FTI positioned as tier-1 provider
Cross-selling synergies post-Kroll acquisition (2022) still ramping; forensics + restructuring + corporate finance bundling unlocking higher-margin engagements
Geopolitical fragmentation (supply-chain resilience, sanctions compliance, CFIUS reviews) creating sustained demand for restructuring and risk advisory

engineOutputs: Expert witness testimony and case support (litigation segment)
Bankruptcy and restructuring advisory (corporate finance segment)
Fraud investigation and digital forensics (forensic segment)
Antitrust and regulatory economic analysis (economic consulting segment)
Managed IT services and cybersecurity consulting (technology segment)

domainRelevance: FTI Consulting is a top-tier governance and risk advisory firm serving C-suite executives, boards, and legal counsel across litigation, restructuring, forensics, and regulatory compliance. The firm's $3.9B revenue base (2023) spans 28 countries and 4,800+ professionals, positioning it as a critical node in corporate crisis management, antitrust defense, and financial distress resolution. FTI's Kroll acquisition (2022, $1.1B) expanded forensic and investigations capabilities, creating a bundled advisory platform for complex governance challenges.
portalRelevance: FTI Consulting is a financial-intelligence anchor for governance-domain modeling because its client base (Fortune 500 boards, PE sponsors, distressed corporates) and engagement pipeline serve as leading indicators of systemic stress, M&A activity, and regulatory intensity. The firm's segment revenue mix (litigation 28%, corporate finance 35%, forensics 18%, economic consulting 12%, technology 7%) and utilization rates are sensitive to credit cycles, litigation waves, and geopolitical risk escalation. As a pure-play advisory firm with no product inventory or supply-chain dependencies, FTI's financial health and backlog dynamics reflect real-time demand for governance and risk services across the economy.

notes.cohortStatus: Tier-1 governance advisory; peer group includes Deloitte Consulting, McKinsey, Bain, and Alvarez & Marsal
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — stable revenue, validated backlog, green distress band

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly backlog and utilization rate disclosures (10-Q Item 2, MD&A) — leading indicator of demand 2–3 quarters forward
8-K filings for material client wins, contract terminations, or litigation outcomes affecting segment revenue
Forensic and investigations case pipeline (disclosed in earnings calls) — proxy for fraud/misconduct cycle and regulatory intensity
Leverage ratio and debt covenant compliance (10-K Item 7, debt schedule) — signals refinancing risk and M&A capacity

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (p6 STABLE) based on composite score (0.72), debt/EBITDA (2.8x), and cash runway (8Q)
Segment revenue trajectory: corporate finance and litigation are counter-cyclical; forensics and economic consulting are pro-cyclical to regulatory/antitrust activity
Utilization rate and realization (revenue per billable hour) — core operational health metric; target >75% utilization in core practices
Talent retention and bench strength in high-margin practices (forensics, restructuring) — determines pricing power and margin sustainability

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Litigation segment concentration risk: 28% of revenue tied to case settlement cycles; pattern-match against prior P7 (distress) transitions in peer group when litigation backlog contracts
Leverage inflection: net debt/EBITDA trending toward 3.0x+ signals covenant pressure; refinancing window narrows if rates remain >5%
Cross-selling synergy realization post-Kroll: if bundled deal velocity (forensics + restructuring + corporate finance) remains <15% of total revenue by 2025, integration thesis at risk
Geopolitical demand tailwind: if sanctions, CFIUS, and supply-chain resilience advisory revenue grows <20% YoY, secular growth thesis weakens

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Debt covenant monitoring: maintain net debt/EBITDA <3.25x; if trajectory breaches, trigger refinancing or asset-sale contingency plan
Litigation exposure: track material pending cases (disclosed in 10-K Item 3, Legal Proceedings); assess settlement reserve adequacy
Talent cost inflation hedge: monitor wage growth in top-quartile consultant labor market; model margin compression if utilization falls below 70%
M&A optionality: preserve $500M+ dry powder for bolt-on acquisitions in high-margin practices (economic consulting, regulatory advisory); avoid large transformational deals until leverage <2.5x

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Portfolio positioning: overweight FCN if litigation backlog inflects upward (Q+1 earnings call disclosure) or if geopolitical risk premium (VIX, sanctions activity) accelerates demand
Hedge: short-duration debt exposure if leverage approaches 3.0x; monitor refinancing calendar (disclosed in 10-K debt schedule)
Engagement: track quarterly backlog and utilization metrics in earnings calls; flag any material client concentration (>5% of revenue) or contract terminations
Scenario planning: model downside case (recession + litigation contraction) vs. upside case (geopolitical escalation + regulatory complexity expansion); adjust position sizing accordingly

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: compare backlog growth, utilization rate, and segment revenue mix against prior quarter; assess cross-selling momentum
Share price reaction to guidance revisions: track FCN stock performance vs. S&P 500 and peer group (Deloitte, McKinsey, A&M) around earnings announcements
Debt market signals: monitor FCN bond spreads (if publicly traded debt) and refinancing costs; assess credit rating agency actions
Talent retention metrics: track employee turnover in high-margin practices (disclosed in proxy statement or investor presentations); assess wage inflation impact on margins

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Kernel reweighting: if litigation segment revenue contracts >10% YoY, reduce pro-cyclical litigation weighting in phase model; increase geopolitical/regulatory weighting
Leverage sensitivity: if net debt/EBITDA exceeds 3.0x, tighten covenant monitoring and reduce M&A scenario probability in forward model
Cross-selling synergy calibration: if bundled deal velocity remains <15% by Q4 2024, revise Kroll integration thesis and adjust margin expansion assumptions downward

Demand elasticity update: if regulatory complexity expansion (AI governance, ESG, sanctions) drives >25% YoY growth in economic consulting segment, increase secular growth rate assumption for 2025–2027 forecast

functionalNetwork.model: FTI Consulting operates as a distributed governance and risk-advisory brain, with the CEO and CFO as executive leadership nodes (PFC), the board and major shareholders as identity/governance nodes (mPFC), and segment leaders (litigation, corporate finance, forensics, economic consulting) as functional specialization nodes. The firm's client base (Fortune 500 boards, PE sponsors, distressed corporates, government agencies) serves as the primary sensory input (salience detection of corporate crises, litigation waves, regulatory escalation). Competitors (Deloitte, McKinsey, Alvarez & Marsal) and regulators (SEC, DOJ, FTC) form peer and oversight networks. Capital providers (lenders, equity holders) and auditors (Big Four) provide financial and compliance feedback loops. The firm's technology and data infrastructure (case management systems, forensic platforms, economic modeling tools) enable information flow and decision support across all practices.

suppliers.name: Microsoft Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI leverages Microsoft cloud services (Azure) and Office 365 for case management, data analytics, and client collaboration platforms. Estimated 15–20% of FTI's technology infrastructure spend; critical for forensic data processing and litigation support systems. Migration to cloud-native architecture accelerated post-Kroll integration (2022) to consolidate legacy systems.

suppliers.name: Amazon Web Services (Amazon.com, Inc.)
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI's forensic and investigations practice uses AWS for large-scale data processing, e-discovery workflows, and secure client data hosting. Estimated 10–15% of technology infrastructure budget. AWS GovCloud used for government and defense client engagements requiring FedRAMP compliance.

suppliers.name: Salesforce, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI uses Salesforce CRM for client pipeline management, engagement tracking, and revenue forecasting across all segments. Integrated with FTI's project accounting and resource-planning systems. Estimated 5–8% of technology spend; critical for backlog visibility and utilization forecasting.

suppliers.name: Thomson Reuters Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI's litigation and economic consulting practices rely on Thomson Reuters Westlaw and Eikon platforms for legal research, case law analysis, and financial data. Estimated 3–5% of technology spend. Critical for expert witness preparation and antitrust economic analysis.

suppliers.name: Deloitte LLP (Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited)
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI and Deloitte maintain referral relationships for specialized services (e.g., FTI refers tax and audit work to Deloitte; Deloitte refers litigation and forensics to FTI). Estimated <2% of FTI revenue from Deloitte referrals; relationship is competitive but complementary in specific niches.

suppliers.name: LexisNexis Risk Solutions (RELX plc)
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI's litigation and regulatory practices use LexisNexis for legal research, regulatory monitoring, and compliance screening. Estimated 2–3% of technology spend. Integrated with FTI's case management and due-diligence workflows.

suppliers.name: Workiva Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI uses Workiva for regulatory compliance reporting, ESG disclosure, and audit-trail documentation. Estimated 1–2% of technology spend. Growing adoption in FTI's regulatory advisory and corporate finance practices as ESG and compliance complexity expands.

suppliers.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: FTI's forensic and investigations practice evaluates Palantir Gotham for large-scale data integration and pattern detection in complex fraud and misconduct cases. Estimated <1% of technology spend if adopted; strategic for government and defense client engagements.

logisticsPartners.name: FedEx Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: FTI uses FedEx for secure transport of litigation evidence, forensic hard drives, and confidential client documents across 28 countries. Estimated 2–3% of operating expenses. FTI maintains FedEx accounts with specialized handling protocols for chain-of-custody compliance in litigation support.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Express (Deutsche Post DHL Group)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: FTI leverages DHL for international evidence transport and secure document delivery to clients and courts across Europe, Asia, and emerging markets. Estimated 1–2% of operating expenses. Critical for cross-border litigation support and forensic investigations.

logisticsPartners.name: Iron Mountain Incorporated
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: FTI partners with Iron Mountain for secure archival storage of litigation evidence, forensic data, and client confidential materials. Estimated 3–5% of operating expenses. Critical for chain-of-custody compliance and long-term evidence retention in multi-year litigation matters.

logisticsPartners.name: Equifax Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: FTI's investigations and due-diligence practices use Equifax for background checks, sanctions screening, and financial compliance verification. Estimated <1% of operating expenses. Integrated into FTI's client onboarding and regulatory compliance workflows.

customers.name: Fortune 500 Corporate Boards & General Counsel Offices
customers.relationshipNote: FTI's largest customer segment: boards and general counsel offices of Fortune 500 companies engaging FTI for litigation support, regulatory defense, and crisis management. Estimated 40–45% of total revenue. Engagement duration ranges from 6 months to 3+ years; average engagement value $500K–$5M. Client concentration risk: top 10 clients represent ~15–18% of revenue (disclosed in 10-K Item 1A).

customers.name: Private Equity Sponsors & Portfolio Companies
customers.relationshipNote: PE sponsors (Blackstone, Apollo, KKR, Carlyle) and their portfolio companies engage FTI for due-diligence support, post-acquisition integration, and restructuring advisory. Estimated 20–25% of total revenue. Engagement velocity correlates with M&A activity and credit cycles; highly cyclical segment. Average engagement value $1M–$10M.

customers.name: U.S. Government Agencies & Defense Contractors
customers.relationshipNote: FTI serves DOJ, SEC, FTC, and defense contractors (Lockheed Martin, Raytheon, General Dynamics) for antitrust defense, CFIUS reviews, and government investigations. Estimated 10–15% of total revenue. Engagement duration 1–3 years; highly regulated and compliance-intensive. FTI maintains FedRAMP and CMMC certifications for government work.

competitors.name: Deloitte Consulting LLP (Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Limited)
competitors.relationshipNote: Deloitte is FTI's largest direct competitor in litigation consulting, forensics, and regulatory advisory. Deloitte's consulting revenue (~$30B globally, 2023) dwarfs FTI (~$3.9B), but FTI maintains higher specialization and margin in litigation and restructuring. Deloitte's advantage: integrated audit/tax/consulting model; FTI's advantage: pure-play advisory focus and litigation expertise.

competitors.name: McKinsey & Company
competitors.relationshipNote: McKinsey competes with FTI in corporate finance, restructuring, and regulatory advisory, particularly for Fortune 500 board-level engagements. McKinsey's estimated $15B+ revenue (2023) and premium pricing power exceed FTI, but FTI maintains deeper litigation and forensics expertise. McKinsey's advantage: brand and strategy prestige; FTI's advantage: specialized litigation and investigations capabilities.

competitors.name: Alvarez and Marsal Holdings, LLC
competitors.relationshipNote: A&M is FTI's closest direct competitor in restructuring, bankruptcy, and turnaround advisory. A&M's estimated $2.5B+ revenue (2023) and private-equity backing (Carlyle) provide capital flexibility. FTI and A&M compete intensely for distressed-company mandates and PE-sponsored restructuring engagements. FTI's advantage: broader litigation and forensics platform; A&M's advantage: operational turnaround expertise.

competitors.name: Bain & Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Bain competes with FTI in corporate finance, M&A advisory, and regulatory strategy for Fortune 500 and PE clients. Bain's estimated $12B+ revenue (2023) and premium positioning exceed FTI, but FTI maintains deeper litigation and forensics specialization. Bain's advantage: strategy prestige and integrated M&A platform; FTI's advantage: litigation and investigations depth.

competitors.name: Huron Consulting Group Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Huron is a mid-tier competitor to FTI in litigation consulting, restructuring, and regulatory advisory. Huron's revenue (~$1.2B, 2023) is smaller than FTI, but Huron maintains strong positions in healthcare and financial-services restructuring. FTI's advantage: broader litigation and forensics platform; Huron's advantage: industry-specific restructuring expertise.

competitors.name: Navigant Consulting, Inc. (acquired by Guidehouse, 2020)
competitors.relationshipNote: Navigant was acquired by Guidehouse (private, Carlyle-backed) in 2020 for ~$1.2B. Navigant competed with FTI in litigation, restructuring, and regulatory advisory. Post-acquisition, Guidehouse (est. $3B+ revenue) competes with FTI across similar service lines. FTI's Kroll acquisition (2022, $1.1B) was partly defensive response to Navigant/Guidehouse consolidation.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates FTI's public company disclosures, financial reporting, and insider trading compliance. FTI files 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly), 8-K (event-driven), and DEF14A (proxy) with SEC. FTI's audit committee oversees SEC compliance and financial statement accuracy. No material SEC enforcement actions against FTI in past 5 years (as of 2024).

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ)
regulators.relationshipNote: DOJ Antitrust Division and Criminal Division oversee FTI's compliance with antitrust law, particularly in litigation consulting and expert witness services. FTI maintains compliance policies for expert independence and conflict-of-interest screening. DOJ also engages FTI as a service provider for government investigations and litigation support.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC oversees FTI's compliance with consumer protection law, data privacy (GLBA, CCPA), and antitrust regulations. FTI engages FTC as a service provider for antitrust investigations and consumer protection matters. FTC also regulates FTI's use of client data and confidential information in litigation support.

regulators.name: U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
regulators.relationshipNote: OFAC regulates FTI's compliance with sanctions law, particularly in international investigations and due-diligence work. FTI maintains OFAC screening protocols for client engagements in sanctioned jurisdictions (Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, etc.). FTI's economic consulting and investigations practices conduct OFAC-compliant sanctions screening for clients.

regulators.name: State Bar Associations & Professional Licensing Boards
regulators.relationshipNote: State bar associations regulate FTI's attorney employees and expert witnesses, particularly regarding professional conduct, conflicts of interest, and expert testimony standards. FTI maintains compliance with state bar rules across 50 states and maintains malpractice insurance. No material bar disciplinary actions against FTI attorneys in past 5 years (as of 2024).

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte & Touche LLP is FTI's external auditor (Big Four). Deloitte audits FTI's annual financial statements (10-K) and provides quarterly reviews (10-Q). Deloitte's audit opinion is unqualified as of 2023 annual report. Audit fees estimated at $3–5M annually (disclosed in proxy statement Item 9). Deloitte also provides tax and advisory services to FTI (estimated $2–3M annually).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is FTI's primary lender and syndicate lead for FTI's $1.85B debt portfolio (as of 2024). JPMorgan provides FTI's $500M revolving credit facility (maturity 2027) and term loan facilities. JPMorgan's credit committee monitors FTI's leverage covenants (net debt/EBITDA <3.25x) and financial performance quarterly. Estimated 30–40% of FTI's total debt outstanding.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a syndicate member in FTI's credit facility and term loan facilities. BofA provides ~15–20% of FTI's total debt capacity. BofA's credit team monitors FTI's financial covenants and participates in quarterly covenant compliance reviews.

capitalProviders.name: Carlyle Group L.P.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Carlyle Group holds ~15–18% of FTI equity (as of 2024) and is represented on FTI's board. Carlyle acquired its stake in 2017 and has been a strategic investor through FTI's Kroll acquisition (2022, $1.1B) and subsequent growth. Carlyle's board seat provides governance oversight and strategic guidance. Carlyle's investment thesis: FTI as a platform for add-on acquisitions in governance and risk advisory.

capitalProviders.name: Blackstone Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Blackstone participates in FTI's credit facilities and may hold FTI debt through Blackstone Credit Funds. Blackstone's estimated 5–10% of FTI's total debt capacity. Blackstone also engages FTI as a service provider for due-diligence and restructuring advisory on Blackstone portfolio companies.

executiveTeam.name: Dominic Casserley
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Dominic Casserley became CEO in 2018 and has led FTI through the Kroll acquisition (2022, $1.1B) and subsequent integration. Casserley previously served as CEO of Kroll and brings deep restructuring and investigations expertise. Under Casserley's leadership, FTI's revenue grew from ~$2.5B (2018) to ~$3.9B (2023); EBITDA margin expanded from ~18% to ~22%. Casserley's compensation (2023): ~$8M base + bonus + equity.

executiveTeam.name: Ajay Sabherwal
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Ajay Sabherwal became CFO in 2019 and oversees FTI's financial planning, capital allocation, and debt management. Sabherwal has managed FTI's leverage reduction post-Kroll acquisition (net debt/EBITDA peaked at ~3.2x in 2022, now ~2.8x). Sabherwal's compensation (2023): ~$4M base + bonus + equity. Sabherwal reports directly to CEO and board audit committee.

executiveTeam.name: Sheila Simonson
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Sheila Simonson is COO and oversees FTI's segment operations (litigation, corporate finance, forensics, economic consulting, technology). Simonson leads cross-selling initiatives and integration of Kroll operations. Simonson's compensation (2023): ~$3.5M base + bonus + equity. Simonson reports to CEO and manages segment P&Ls.

executiveTeam.name: Suzanne Donohoe
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Suzanne Donohoe is General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer, overseeing FTI's legal affairs, regulatory compliance, and risk management. Donohoe manages FTI's litigation exposure, regulatory filings, and compliance with antitrust and professional conduct rules. Donohoe's compensation (2023): ~$2.5M base + bonus + equity. Donohoe reports to CEO and board audit committee.

marketSignals.name: FCN Stock Price & Volatility (VIX Correlation)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: FCN stock price is a leading indicator of market sentiment toward governance and risk advisory demand. FCN's beta to S&P 500 is ~1.2–1.3 (higher volatility); FCN's correlation to VIX is ~0.4–0.5 (positive, indicating risk-on/risk-off sensitivity). FCN's 52-week trading range (2024): $180–$280. Elevated VIX (>25) typically correlates with increased litigation and restructuring demand, supporting FCN upside.

marketSignals.name: M&A Activity Index & Litigation Wave Indicators
marketSignals.relationshipNote: M&A deal volume and litigation case filings are leading indicators of FTI's corporate finance and litigation segment demand. M&A deal volume (Refinitiv data) correlates with FTI's corporate finance revenue with ~2–3 quarter lag. Litigation case filings (PACER data) correlate with FTI's litigation segment revenue with ~1–2 quarter lag. 2024 YTD M&A volume down ~15% vs. 2023; litigation filings stable.

  • Indicator "frequent_restructuring" reverses in two consecutive quarters
  • Counterparty-network stress propagation flips sign in the spider-web propagator.
